operations.name: Handshake
operations.carries: The envelope version range the client speaks.
operations.consumer: dwkd-authority connection setup (M3), which also enforces that it is the first message.
operations.second_path: It negotiates how later messages are encoded and nothing else. It names no resource, carries no capability and grants no authority: every later request is still individually decoded, canonicalised and policed. The receiver's version floor stops it being used to downgrade the connection.

operations.name: Heartbeat
operations.carries: Envelope session_id and epoch only; an empty payload.
operations.second_path: It can only extend authority the kernel already granted, by at most one lease TTL, and only while the stated epoch is the kernel's current one; a stale epoch is fenced (PROTOCOL.md section 3). It names no resource and cannot create, widen or transfer authority. The epoch it carries is one the kernel issued, compared against kernel.db, never believed.

operations.name: AcquireLease
operations.carries: Envelope session_id; an empty payload. The response carries the kernel-assigned epoch.
operations.second_path: The sender cannot propose an epoch; the kernel assigns it. A lease confers the right to write one session and nothing more: capabilities come only from AdmitRun, so holding a lease authorises no effect. Its only external consequence is fencing other writers of the same session, which is its purpose. M3 adds the policy denial for a session the caller may not lease; a protocol error is not that denial.

operations.name: ReleaseLease
operations.carries: Envelope session_id and epoch; an empty payload.
operations.second_path: It can only surrender authority, never gain it, and only for a lease held at the stated current epoch. It names nothing but the session.

operations.name: AdmitRun
operations.carries: Agent profile and requested skills; response RunGrant{run_id, capability_tokens[], budget_lease, epoch}.
operations.consumer: Capability Broker and Budget Ledger (M3, M6).
operations.second_path: When defined: the grant is minted kernel-side from agent profile, kernel-verified skills, parent grant and profile ceiling; nothing the runtime asserts is a term in that expression (ADR-0028, invariant I9). Payload deferred to M3 because the capability token format does not exist yet.

operations.name: ReleaseRun
operations.carries: run_id; response Ack.
operations.second_path: When defined: can only end authority, never extend it.

operations.name: ToolInvoke
operations.carries: A typed tool invocation and capability token; responses ToolResult, Denial or ApprovalPending.
operations.consumer: Canonicaliser, policy, capabilities, approvals, budget, audit; then a per-invocation authorisation to dwkd-broker.
operations.second_path: This IS the path from cognition to effect; there must be no other. When defined it must name a tool from the canonical inventory with typed arguments the kernel canonicalises itself; it must never accept an opaque command, script or frame.

operations.name: ToolCancel
operations.carries: Invocation id; response Ack.
operations.second_path: When defined: can only stop an effect already authorised, never start one.

operations.name: ModelCall
operations.carries: Typed ModelCall{provider_profile_id, model, messages[], tool_schemas[], sampling_params} (ADR-0020); streamed deltas or Denial.
operations.consumer: Authority (origin, privacy class, credential, budget); dwkd-broker renders the HTTP request from a declarative provider profile.
operations.second_path: When defined it must carry semantics only: no URL, header, credential, raw body or endpoint, which is how ADR-0002's HttpRequestSpec became an unpoliced network capability. Open for M7: ADR-0020 lists privacy_class in the request while ADR-0028 makes privacy_class a kernel-derived policy input; M7 must either drop it from the request or accept it only as a request to narrow.

operations.name: CanonicalPreview
operations.carries: A proposed tool invocation; response CanonicalAction.
operations.consumer: direwolf policy simulate; the approval [w]hy branch.
operations.second_path: When defined: resolves what an action would mean without performing it, so the untrusted side never duplicates canonicalisation. It must not reserve, lock or touch the resource.

operations.name: CreateArtifact
operations.carries: Streamed content; response ArtifactId.
operations.consumer: Kernel-side content-addressed store with kernel-assigned provenance.
operations.second_path: When defined: writes only into the kernel-owned CAS, quota-bounded, with trust assigned by the kernel. It must never accept a destination path or a provenance label from the runtime.

operations.name: ReadArtifact
operations.carries: ArtifactId; streamed bytes.
operations.second_path: When defined: reads by content id from the kernel's store only; never a path.

operations.name: QueryBudget
operations.carries: Run id; response BudgetSnapshot.
operations.second_path: When defined: read-only.

operations.name: QueryAuthority
operations.carries: Run id; response EffectiveAuthority.
operations.second_path: When defined: read-only; reports authority, grants none.

operations.name: QueryInvocationStatus
operations.carries: Idempotency key; response the audited outcome (RELIABILITY.md section 1).
operations.consumer: Crash recovery (M9), answering from the audit chain.
operations.second_path: When defined: read-only. It answers whether an effect happened; it never re-performs one.

operations.name: ListVisibleTools
operations.carries: Run id; response ToolDefinition[] fixed at admission (ADR-0026).
operations.second_path: When defined: read-only; visibility can only narrow after admission.

operations.name: SpawnSubagent
operations.carries: Parent run and requested attenuation; response RunGrant.
operations.second_path: When defined it must remain expressible as AdmitRun plus an attenuation request (ADR-0029); if it ever needs more, the primitive layer has leaked.

operations.name: McpOpen
operations.carries: MCP server identity; response McpServerHandle and ToolDefinition[].
operations.consumer: Kernel-owned MCP client; dwkd-broker spawns the server sandboxed.
operations.second_path: The kernel owns the MCP protocol, not merely the process. There is no operation that relays a frame; invoking a discovered tool is an ordinary ToolInvoke. McpSend/McpRecv were a second path found in Phase 0 and must never return.

operations.name: McpClose
operations.carries: McpServerHandle; response Ack.
operations.second_path: When defined: can only stop a server.

operations.name: ChannelSend
operations.carries: Typed outbound message; response DeliveryReceipt.
operations.consumer: Secret broker (channel credential) and egress policy.
operations.second_path: Outbound delivery goes through the kernel because the channel token is a credential and outbound content is an egress surface. When defined, the destination is a configured channel reference, never a URL or token supplied by the runtime.
